A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the phage head is assembled by a complex of phage and host components, which includes the major head protein (gene E product), a protein which is converted to a lower mol wt form during assembly (B or C gene product), and an unidentified protein which is provided by the host.
the groE gene product is involved in the conversion of the protein encoded by head gene B to h3, and that this conversion is required before the protein encoded by gene E can assemble into a head.
the groE gene product is a protein which is required for the assembly of the phage E, B, and C proteins into the phage head.
The main takeaway from our work is that
phage head assembly requires the cooperation of the phage and host.
host participation in head assembly is not limited to a role in the formation of the head shell.
host participation in bacteriophages is a very common occurrence and it is not limited to a few specific phages.
